sources.title: How does washing detergent work?
sources.publication: Royal Society of Chemistry Education, sections How do detergents work? and Washing clothes

evidence.note: University of Washington defines saponification as alkaline hydrolysis of glyceryl trialkanoates forming glycerol and salts of long-chain carboxylic acids. It gives no ash concentration, heating protocol, historical availability or cleaning outcome.

anchor.section: How do detergents work?; Washing clothes

evidence.note: RSC describes hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails surrounding oil/grease in micelles, which can then be washed away. It does not establish a soap amount, textile, water, stain, agitation, complete removal or preservation outcome.

object.value: alkaline hydrolysis of triglycerides forms glycerol and salts of long-chain fatty acids that are soaps
an amphiphilic cleaning molecule can surround oil or grease with hydrophobic tails inward and hydrophilic heads outward, dispersing it in water for removal

concept_localizations.short_definition: Общие химические механизмы образования и действия мыла.
General chemical mechanisms of soap formation and cleaning.

claim_localizations.runtime_text: Щелочной гидролиз триглицеридов образует глицерин и соли длинноцепочечных жирных кислот — мыла.
Alkaline hydrolysis of triglycerides forms glycerol and salts of long-chain fatty acids that are soaps.
Амфифильное очищающее вещество может окружать масло или жир гидрофобными хвостами внутрь и гидрофильными головками наружу, диспергируя его в воде для удаления.
An amphiphilic cleaning molecule can surround oil or grease with hydrophobic tails inward and hydrophilic heads outward, dispersing it in water for removal.
